stories.title: Overseas education project for women and girls axed by UK after two years
bullet_points: The programme, aimed at keeping 1m girls in school across Africa, Asia and the Middle East, withdrawn after aid cuts  A leading higher education programme, aimed at keeping 1 million girls in school across Africa, Asia and the Middle East, has been axed by the British government just two years after it was announced.

The scheme, Strengthening higher education for female empowerment (SHEFE), which was  unveiled with some fanfare  two years ago by the outgoing Conservative government, had a £45m budget to increase access to higher education for 1 million students worldwide.
It has now had its tender withdrawn, the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) said.
